resume.title: Resume
resume.description: Your resume as a PDF file, up to 5 MB.

entry.title: Entry
entry.description: One work_history, sections or education entry, copied exactly as written there.

type.title: Type
type.description: What kind of experience the entry is. Paid employment is 'job'; personal, academic or employer-unspecified projects are 'project'.

end.title: End
end.description: When the entry ended as YYYY-MM, 'present' if ongoing, or empty if the entry gives no date.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One sentence written like a job-posting responsibility, using only what the entry says. No company, product or award names, dates, money figures, or notes such as 'context not specified'.

hard_skills.title: Hard Skills
hard_skills.description: Programming languages, frameworks, libraries, platforms, tools and techniques the entry shows were used, named the way job postings list requirements. Include the language a named framework or library is written in. Leave out features or results of what was built, metrics and task descriptions, and anything the entry does not support.

soft_skills.title: Soft Skills
soft_skills.description: Soft skills the entry shows through a described action, each named with the common term job postings use (for example 'Mentoring' for 'mentored two interns'), not a coined phrase. Never list one without such an action.

section_headings.title: Section Headings
section_headings.description: Every section heading in the resume, in order, exactly as written. List them before filling the other fields so no section is skipped.

sections.title: Sections
sections.description: Every other resume section under its own heading, for example Projects, Certifications, Publications, Volunteering, Awards, Research, Leadership or Languages. Leave out what is already in work_history, education, skills or the summary, and contact details. Evidence of skills, never of employment years.

tech_skills.title: Tech Skills
tech_skills.description: List of Familiar Programming Languages or Frameworks (e.g. Python, C++, JavaScript, Java, ReactJS, NodeJS)

skill_groups.title: Skill Groups
skill_groups.description: Every tech_skills entry placed in exactly one group of related skills, so each group describes one kind of work.

keyword_queries.title: Keyword Queries
keyword_queries.description: One or two lines of 6-12 space-separated terms from tech_skills for exact matching against job ads, most important first, for example 'Python FastAPI React PostgreSQL Docker'. Use names employers list; no soft skills, no terms the resume does not support.

soft_skills.title: Soft Skills
soft_skills.description: List of Soft skills (e.g. Responsibility, Curiosity, Leadership)

entry_evidence.title: Entry Evidence
entry_evidence.description: One item per work_history, sections and education entry: what was done there and the hard and soft skills it demonstrates.

years_of_experience.title: Years Of Experience
years_of_experience.description: Completed years of paid professional employment, excluding degree duration, coursework and personal/academic projects. Avoid double-counting overlapping dates. Do not round internships up to full years.

career_level.title: Career Level
career_level.description: Career level supported by professional scope and tenure, not degree level or technology keywords.

experience_evidence.title: Experience Evidence
experience_evidence.description: Brief resume evidence for employment tenure and responsibility; explicitly identify internships and academic work.

preferred_domains.title: Preferred Domains
preferred_domains.description: Three to six realistic job titles to search for now, inferred from the whole resume (work history, sections, education and skills) at the candidate's career level, for example 'Graduate Data Analyst' or 'Junior Python Developer', including common variants employers use for the same work. Include a stated interest only when the resume supports it.

target_roles_reason.title: Target Roles Reason
target_roles_reason.description: One or two sentences on why these job titles fit, citing the resume evidence and career level.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: A brief summary of candidate's professional bacground and academic focus

heading.title: Heading
heading.description: The section heading exactly as the resume writes it.

entries.title: Entries
entries.description: Each item in the section as 'Title | Context | Month Year – Month Year | Details', keeping only the parts the resume gives, with its tools, scope and outcomes.

name.title: Name
name.description: A short area of work, for example 'LLM applications', 'Backend' or 'Data analysis'.

skills.title: Skills
skills.description: Skills from tech_skills, written exactly as listed there.

query.title: Query
query.description: One 15-35 word sentence a job ad would use for this kind of work, for example 'Build and deploy backend REST APIs using Python, FastAPI and PostgreSQL.' Name the mainstream tools employers list and describe niche models or tools by their category ('U-Net' becomes 'image segmentation models'). Leave out project, dataset and domain details, team words such as 'collaboratively', and work the resume does not show.

resume_quotes.title: Resume Quotes
resume_quotes.description: Every short verbatim resume passage that supports this verdict, usually one to three, from any section; empty when the resume does not mention the requirement.
